[Cp*RhCl2]2 catalyzed three-component coupling
cyclization of 2,3-allenoic acids with 2,3-allenols
in the presence of Cu(OAc) 2·H2O†
Junjie Fan,
 Xiaoyan Wu,
 Chunling Fu and Shengming Ma
 *
Here we report a [Cp*RhCl 2]2 catalyzed three-component coupling cyclization of 2,3-allenoic acids and
2,3-allenols in the presence of Cu(OAc) 2·H2O, a ﬀording furanone derivatives. The synthetic potential has
been demonstrated. The mechanism has also been demonstrated by isotopic labeling experiments,
unveiling unexpected reaction pathways.
Introduction
Allenes have been developed as versatile building blocks in
organic syntheses. 1,2 Our group has developed the Rh/Cu co-
catalyzed homo-coupling cyclization of 2,3-allenols 1,
aﬀording a dihydrofuran ring linked with a conjugated enone
unit ( E)-2 (Scheme 1a). 3 The Rh catalyzed cross-coupling cycli-
zation reaction of 2,3-allenoic acids 3 in the presence of 2,3-
allenols 1 aﬀording furan-2(5 H)-ones ( E)-4 has also been
reported (Scheme 1b). 4 Here we wish to report a three-com-
ponent coupling cyclization of 2,3-allenoic acids 3 in the pres-
ence of 2,3-allenols 1 and Cu(OAc) 2·H2O catalyzed by a Rh( III)
catalyst forming a new type of furan-2(5 H)-one 5 via unique
mechanisms (Scheme 1c).
Results and discussion
Initially, the three-component coupling cyclization reaction
was tried using 2,3-allenoic acid 3a (0.2 mmol) and 2,3-allenol
1a (0.3 mmol) in the presence of [Cp*RhCl
2]2 (7.5 mol%) and
Cu(OAc)2·H2O (0.6 mmol) in CH 3CN (0.6 mL)/methanol
(30 μL) under an oxygen atmosphere (Scheme 2-1). 3 The reac-
tion a ﬀorded the homo-coupling product ( E)-2a in 12% NMR
yield derived from two molecules of 2,3-allenol 1a. In addition,
two formal 1,4-conjugate addition products of ( E)-4aa with
acetate, 5aa (30% yield by NMR) and 6aa (8% yield by NMR),
were detected. However, interestingly, when ( E)-4aa was pre-
pared on purpose and then treated under the same catalytic
conditions with [Cp*RhCl
2]2 (5 mol%) and Cu(OAc) 2·H2O( 2
equiv.) for 12 h, 5aa was not formed (Scheme 2-2), indicating a
unique mechanism for the formation of 5aa and 6aa.
To optimize the selectivity, we adjusted the ratio of 3a/1a
from 1/1.5 to 1.5/1 and observed that the yield of 5aa was
improved and the formation of ( E)-2a was not observed
(Table 1, entries 2 and 3). Interestingly, further increasing the
loading of 3a improved the selectivity of 5aa/6aa (entry 4). The
reaction in open air gave similar results (entry 5 vs. entry 4).
Surprisingly, when the reaction was conducted in an inert
atmosphere of N
2, 5aa was formed exclusively (entry 6). Upon
studying the e ﬀects of Cu(OAc) 2·H2O loading and concen-
tration (entries 7 –10), the conditions described in entry 9 were

To clarify the mechanism, a control experiment was con-
ducted. In the absence of the rhodium catalyst, the reaction
failed to a ﬀord 5aa (Scheme 3-1), indicating that [Cp*RhCl
2]2
was crucial. In the absence of Cu(OAc) 2·H2O with O 2 as the
oxidant and NaOAc as the acetoxylation agent, the reaction
aﬀorded 5aa in only 8% NMR yield and 6aa in 5% NMR yield
(Scheme 3-2), whereas with KOAc as the acetoxylation agent,
the reaction a ﬀorded 6aa in 5% NMR yield but not 5aa, with
48% recovery of 1a (Scheme 3-3), indicating the importance of
Cu(OAc)
2·H2O. The reaction of allenoic acid 3a and deuterated
allenol [D]- 1a (>99% D) a ﬀorded [D]- 5aa, with the methyl
group connected to the α-carbon atom of acetoxy being mono-
deuterated (Scheme 3-4). With an additional 20 equivalents of
D
2O and using MeOD instead of MeOH, the reaction of 1a and
3a aﬀorded the α-deuterated product [D] ′-5aa (82% D) in 38%
yield (Scheme 3-5). When 20 equivalents of D 2O were added
after the completion of the reaction of 1a and 3a under the
standard conditions, 5aa was isolated in 45% yield without
any deuterium incorporation (Scheme 3-6), indicating that
[D]′-5aa was not produced by 5aa directly.
Based on these experimental results and the literature,
3–5
two mechanisms were proposed, as shown in Scheme 4. First,
[Cp*RhCl2]2 would undergo ligand exchange to a ﬀord
Cp*RhOAc2.6 Then allenoic acid 3 underwent a nucleophilic
cyclic oxyrhodation to a ﬀord the 2-oxo-2,5-dihydrofuran-4-yl-
rhodium intermediate IN-1. Subsequently, [D]- 1 underwent
insertion into the C –Rh bond to generate the stereo-defined
allylic rhodium intermediate IN-2. In path A, the coordination
of the hydroxyl group would be replaced with that of the C –D
bond to form IN-3. The subsequent attack on the fully substi-
tuted sp 2 carbon center by AcO −, which was dissociated or co-
ordinated on Rh( III), would induce the migration of the C vC
bond and D-delivery to a ﬀord IN-4. Reductive elimination of
IN-4 would produce Cp*Rh( I) and IN-5, which would interact
with D 2Ot oa ﬀord [D]- 5. Finally, the Rh( III) species would be
regenerated to complete the catalytic cycle via the oxidation of

Cp*Rh(I) with Cu( II).7 There is an alternative mechanism (Path
B):8 the allylic rhodium intermediate IN-2′ may undergo β-D
elimination to a ﬀord IN-3′. Then the terminal C vC bond
would insert into the Rh-D bond to produce IN-4′. Then the
C–OAc moiety of IN-5 was formed by reductive elimination.
After unveiling the unique mechanism, we explored the
substrate scope of this three-component coupling cyclization
of 2,3-allenoic acids with 2,3-allenols for the formation of pro-
ducts 5 (Table 2). n-Propyl or n-butyl substituted allenoic acids
were first examined, generating the corresponding products
5aa–5lb and 5mb in moderate yields. Allenoic acids equipped
with synthetically versatile groups, such as 3-chloropropyl ( 3c),
allyl ( 3d), and phenethyl ( 3e), could all react with allenols
forming the corresponding products 5ad, 5ae, 5mc, and 5me
in 37% –51% yields. For allenols, R
2 could be 1°-, 2°-, and 3°-
alkyl groups, a ﬀording 5aa–5ea in 37%–67% yields. Functional
groups such as chlorine ( 5fa) and even free hydroxyl ( 5gb) were
also tolerated. R 2 may also be di ﬀerent aryls, a ﬀording the
corresponding products 5ha–5kb in 42% –49% yields.
Gratifyingly, the heteroaryl substrate 1l also matched with alle-
noic acid 3b aﬀording 5lb in 46% yield. Simple buta-2,3-dien-
1-ol ( 1m) could also work to a ﬀord a series of aldehydes 5ma–
5me, leaving new opportunities for further synthetic
elaboration.
To further explore the synthetic utility of this methodology
(Scheme 5), the reaction was conducted on the 8 mmol scale
to a ﬀord product 5ma. 5ma is synthetically versatile: (i) it
reacted with the Wittig reagent to a ﬀord the corresponding
enoate, which was subsequently hydrogenated with RANEY®-
Ni to a ﬀord 7 in 63% combined yield in two steps; (ii) the alde-
hyde unit in 5ma may be selectively reduced to the primary
alcohol 8 with NaBH
3CN; (iii) in the presence of triethylamine,
a highly strained four-membered ring 9 in 9 may be formed.
Subsequent one-pot reduction with NaBH 4 aﬀorded 1,3-diol 10

Conclusions
In conclusion, the [Cp*RhCl 2]2 catalyzed three-component
coupling cyclization of 2,3-allenoic acids and 2,3-allenols
aﬀording furanone derivatives with an acetate functionality
was established. The synthetic potential of the products has
been well demonstrated. The reaction proceeded via nucleo-
philic cyclic oxyrhodation, insertion, and 1,4-H delivery pro-
moted by the addition of AcO
− or a β-H elimination –insertion
mechanism, as unveiled by mechanistic studies.
